unmapped_findings: The 19Al alloy (Fe 41.6, Mn 34.8, Al 18.6, Cu 5.0 at.% by EDS; density 6.66 g/cm³) aged at 650 °C for 6 h is the exact condition used in EBSD Fig. 6(c) where the phase map is uniform green β-Mn with dispersed fine red particles annotated 'New BCC phase'.

Although this sample (19Al, 650 °C/6 h) has a Vickers hardness of 810.9 HV, the peak hardness of the 19Al alloy (917.8 HV) was achieved at 600 °C for 10 h — a different aging condition, and the fracture-toughness (3.5 MPa·m^1/2) and nanoindentation measurements were made on that hardest state, not on the 650 °C/6 h sample.

For the 19Al alloy, the α→β-Mn transformation needed 10 h at 550 °C and was complete after only 1 h at 600 °C and above; the optimum aging temperature range for achieving ultra-high hardness was 575–625 °C.

Increasing Al content slowed the precipitation kinetics of β-Mn (attributed to Al enrichment around β-Mn hindering growth, and to the Al-stabilized D0₃ phase) and decreased the ductile FCC Cu-rich phase between β-Mn interfaces, thereby lowering the final hardening effect and fracture toughness.
